newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine and Romania fail to finalise treaty text.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine and Romania fail to finalise treaty text.

text.p: Ukraine and Romania have failed to agree a long-awaited political accord that Bucharest needs to improve its chances of joining NATO, Kiev's top negotiator said on Friday.

Ukraine's First Deputy Foreign Minister Anton Buteiko told a news conference held after talks on a bilateral friendship treaty in Kiev earlier this week that the two countries had made progress but were still split on some issues.
"The talks were hard but fruitful and constructive. We made significant progress," Buteiko said. "But some elements haven't been agreed yet."
Buteiko did not specify which differences remained but made clear that the rest of the pact could be agreed on the expert level, without formal negotiations.

The talks, in their ninth round, stalled when Romania insisted that Ukraine acknowledge some blame for the former Soviet Union's seizure of chunks of Romanian territory in 1944 under the Nazi-Soviet pact. Ukraine refuses to take any blame.

Romanian officials said earlier this week that their main concern had shifted to agreeing Black Sea borders. Ukraine wants an unequivocal statement that neither side will make territorial claims after an agreement is reached.
Romania's new centrist leadership, which has made quick entry into NATO its main foreign policy goal, has also signalled it is willing to make compromises to secure a deal with Kiev.

Western leaders have praised Romania's conclusion last year of a treaty with Hungary and say its bid to beat the odds and win quick admission to NATO alongside Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, depends on a similar accord with Ukraine.
